# Remove-ZbxRole

## SYNOPSIS

Removes user roles.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxRole [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixRole>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A user role sets what its users may see and do: the user type, the frontend sections, the API methods and the actions they may run. The Remove-ZbxRole cmdlet deletes the user roles given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with role.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a user role

```powershell
Remove-ZbxRole -InputObject 'Read-only operators' -Confirm:$false
```

Deletes the user role Read-only operators. -Confirm:$false skips the prompt the command shows by default.

### Example 2: Preview deleting the user roles a search finds

```powershell
Get-ZbxRole -Name 'Read*' | Remove-ZbxRole -WhatIf
```

Lists the user roles whose names start with Read that the command would delete, and deletes nothing.

Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
